findings.description: Team collective destination calendars lost when primary calendar is null — Attendees lose team destinations and bookings fall back to a single calendar. Initialize `evt.destinationCalendar` from `teamDestinationCalendars` when it is `null` instead of gating `push` with optional chaining.

Hard-coded English calendar note bypasses localization — Attendees see English text regardless of locale. Wrap `calEvent.additionalNotes` with the translation helper used nearby like `getTranslation` instead of the hard-coded literal.

TypeError on undefined destinationCalendar in Google Meet fallback check — Bookings crash with a TypeError when no destination calendar exists. Guard `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration` with optional chaining like `evt.destinationCalendar` previously did.

Inverted fallback makes selectedCalendar undefined when externalCalendarId falsy — The fallback never matches and leaves `selectedCalendar` undefined, so events land on the wrong calendar or fail. Resolve `externalCalendarId` from `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.externalId` instead of searching `destinationCalendar` for the falsy value.

Inverted IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED check sets slug on wrong path — Organizations get a direct `slug` when billing is enabled and break the request flow. Restore the `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` guard for `slug` so `requestedSlug` is used when the flag is on.

Calendar.createEvent credentialId breaks existing implementations — All calendar integrations fail type checks and keep writing to `destinationCalendar[0]`. Update `Calendar.createEvent` implementors to accept `credentialId` and select the matching `destinationCalendar` entry.

Calendar sync uses caller credentials instead of organizer credentials — Using `ctx.user` credentials for `EventManager` means an attendee invite fails to update the organizer's `destinationCalendar`. Load credentials with `getUsersCredentials` for `booking.userId` instead.

DB attendees persisted before external calendar update without compensation — Persisting with `prisma.booking.update` before `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees` leaves orphaned attendees if the calendar call fails. Update the calendar first or add compensation, following `editLocation.handler` ordering.

Organizer lookup throws unhandled 500 when booking.userId is null — When `booking.userId` is null, `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow` with `|| 0` throws an unhandled 500. Check `booking.userId` first and throw a `TRPCError` with `NOT_FOUND` if missing, using `findFirst` instead.

Case-sensitive blacklist and duplicate checks allow bypass via casing — `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` is lowercased but `guest` and `attendee.email` comparisons stay case-sensitive, so `Admin@example.com` bypasses the block and duplicates slip in. Normalize both sides with `toLowerCase()` and `trim()` before checking `blacklistedGuestEmails` and `booking.attendees`.

Team permission check requires both admin and owner instead of either — Using `&&` between `isTeamAdmin` and `isTeamOwner` denies admins who aren't owners and vice versa. Change `isTeamAdminOrOwner` to use `||` to match the `||` pattern in `teams/get.handler` and `confirm.handler`.

Unguarded attendees[0].name access crashes email when attendees empty — An empty list makes `attendees[0].name` throw and the organizer email never sends. Guard `this.calEvent.attendees[0]?.name` and fall back to `this.calEvent.organizer.name`.

handleAdd sends empty and unnormalized emails without trimming/lowercasing — Empty strings and case-variant duplicates in `multiEmailValue` pass the client check but fail or duplicate on the server. Normalize with `trim()` and `toLowerCase()`, filter empty entries, and initialize `multiEmailValue` as `[]` before validation.

Unbounded guests array enables resource exhaustion — An unbounded `guests` array lets one request create many database rows and trigger many emails. Cap `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` with `.max(25)` and enforce the same limit in the handler.

Race condition creates duplicate Attendee rows on concurrent addGuests — Concurrent calls compute `uniqueGuests` from stale `booking.attendees` and both `prisma.booking.update` with `createMany` insert duplicate rows. Use `prisma.$transaction` with `Serializable` isolation and `skipDuplicates` or add a unique index on `bookingId` and `email`.

Duplicate guest emails pass validation causing unique-constraint violation — Duplicate addresses in `guests` pass `ZAddGuestsInputSchema` and make `createMany` hit a unique-constraint error. Add a `.refine` that checks `new Set` size on lowercased and trimmed emails or dedupe with a `Set` before insert.

sendAddGuestsEmails uses unfiltered guests instead of uniqueGuests — Passing `guests` to `sendAddGuestsEmails` instead of `uniqueGuests` emails existing and blacklisted addresses as if new. Call `sendAddGuestsEmails` with `uniqueGuests` so its `newGuests.includes` check matches the persisted attendees.

Literal placeholder for missing refresh_token corrupts credential — Most providers omit `refresh_token` on refresh, so storing the literal corrupts the credential and the next refresh fails with `invalid_grant`. Preserve the existing token instead of hardcoding a placeholder, or delete the field as in the fix.

Missing prisma import causes ReferenceError in Salesforce CalendarService — The integration throws a `ReferenceError` at runtime on every construction because `prisma` is not defined in this file. Add an import for `prisma` from `@calcom/prisma` or use a dynamic import as shown.

Zoho Bigin passes credentialId instead of userId to refreshOAuthTokens — The sync endpoint receives the wrong identifier and cannot locate the correct credential because `credentialId` is passed where `userId` is expected. Pass `credential.userId` to `refreshOAuthTokens` instead of `credentialId` to match `calcomUserId` like other callers.

Malformed minimumTokenResponseSchema rejects all valid token refresh responses — When `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` every valid response is rejected because `minimumTokenResponseSchema` requires literal `ZodString`/`ZodOptional` keys and strips unknowns. Replace the computed keys with `z.object({ access_token: z.string() }).passthrough()` as in the fix.

Google credential update persists SafeParseResult wrapper instead of data — The stored `key` becomes the wrapper `{success, data, error}` so later credential use fails. Unwrap the `parseRefreshTokenResponse` result, check `success`, and persist only `data` before `prisma.credential.update`.

Lark refresh validates sync OAuth response as Lark envelope and fails — Sync responses contain `access_token` not the Lark `{code, msg}` envelope, so `handleLarkError` always throws. Branch on the shape: only call `handleLarkError` for `code`-bearing payloads and normalize `access_token` responses separately.

Sync branch returns fetch Response instead of provider token shape — Callers like Google read `token.access_token` via `res.data`, so a raw `Response` causes `TypeError` and breaks sync for all providers. Parse `fetch` JSON and normalize to `{data, ...token}` so `refreshOAuthTokens` matches provider shapes.
